newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Feb 21.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - Moderate sales left mills optimistic and secondaries circumspect about the market's near-term prospects, Random Lengths said in its weekly update. While mild weather across much of the nation spurred shipments and job site activity, resistance to current prices was widespread, it said.

Many wholesalers, uncertain of the market's strength, stuck to back to back purchases. Sales at most mills kept pace with production, though, and prices ended Thursday on an upward tilt. Thursday's news of a modest move upward in January housing starts was received with little fanfare, Random Lengths said.

Producers approached the market firmly, optimistic about prospects for a round of spring buying. They gave ground reluctantly to move must-sell loadings but were confident that any future downward price adjustments would be minor and short-lived. Meanwhile, dealers purchased selectively, buying just enough to cover their most pressing needs and little more.

Dealers often turned first to wholesalers offering quick shiments and more competitive prices. Recognizing the price resistance among dealers, wholesalers turned speculative purchases quickly at modest profits, Random Lengths said.

The Presidents Day holiday on Monday contributed to the week's slow start. A drying trend improved the prospects for logging in parts of the South, although rains continued to soak the westside zone. Radius edge decking and timbers remained the strongest items in the South. Western Canadian mills continued to fight railcar supply problems. But some distributors reported that long-delayed shipments finally began to reach destinations.
Low-grade dimension supplies were tight and Economy posted solid gains in several species. Western Red Cedar prices showed little sign of losing momentum, Random Lengths said.
Canadian imports as of February 12 were at 49.8 percent of the January-March fee-free quota and 90.9 pct of the annual April/March quota, the reporting agency said.
